lines.text: `digest` prints one line per changed file (kind, hunks, symbols), `show` prints the patch for one hunk or file, and `pregroup` writes a draft review (identical copies, mechanical files, one change group).
When the branch gets new commits or a rebase, the review does not start over:
```sh
comprehende refresh --data review.json

`review` and `pregroup` record the commits the refs resolved to in `source.baseSha` and `source.headSha`. `refresh` resolves the refs again, keeps every hunk whose path and changed lines are unchanged (re-pointing its ref when only the start moved), keeps an edited hunk in its group and marks it changed, drops refs whose hunk left the diff, and puts hunks no group covers into a draft `update` group. It prints the new commit subjects and one line per changed file, so the skill rewrites only the groups that changed. `serve` and `export` print a note when the refs no longer resolve to the recorded commits.
## Release
Edit the skill in `skills-next/comprehende/`. `npx skills add` reads `skills/comprehende/` only.
**Stale ref.** Pointer that does not match live git. Serve still starts. Do not invent a replacement.

**Refresh.** Carry a review over to new commits. A hunk with the same path and the same added and removed lines is the same hunk; its ref follows it. A hunk edited in the same region of the file is changed and keeps its group; its prose is re-checked. Any other hunk is new or gone. `source.baseSha` and `source.headSha` record where the last review stood.
**Skill.** Grouping instructions. Does not talk to git.
**CLI.** review, validate, serve, export. Cwd is the repo. `review` writes a covering skeleton only; the skill fills interpretation.
**CLI.** review, pregroup, digest, show, refresh, validate, serve, export. Cwd is the repo. `review` and `pregroup` write a covering draft only; the skill fills interpretation.
